title: Sitrus Perch Link
premise: A small neon-horror sci-fi interaction scene where the player taps perched drones to surface chatter, trigger Sitrus-specific glitches, and soak in an eerie ambient mood.
interaction_model: Single-screen tap/click interaction on a canvas scene with HUD overlays; tap characters for randomized dialogue and tap empty space for ambient ripple particles.
objective: Explore the perch scene, reveal character dialogue, and trigger Sitrus's glitch reaction for audiovisual feedback rather than pursue a formal win state.
progression: Very light progression: the session opens from a start screen into a persistent loop of tapping, dialogue discovery, and temporary glitch states, with no levels, scoring, or unlocks visible.
theme: Cyber-horror drone perch vignette with fandom-style character banter, snowy stillness, and unstable signal aesthetics.
mood: Moody, playful, eerie, neon, slightly unsettling, and atmospheric.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy short interactive toys, character-centric fandom experiences, ambient sci-fi presentation, and low-pressure tap interactions.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a one-screen tap interaction built around dialogue and glitch feedback.
High confidence there is no formal scoring, win/lose state, or stage progression in the current code.
Moderate confidence that the work is fandom-inspired because of character naming and quoted dialogue references.
Lower confidence on any intended broader narrative because the code only exposes ambient interactions and short voice-line-style text.
recreation_prompt: Create a one-screen browser game called "Sitrus Perch Link" presented as a neon sci-fi snowy perch scene on an HTML5 canvas with a DOM HUD overlay and a dramatic start screen. The player should press a single start button to open the link, begin ambient background audio, and enter a calm but eerie interactive vignette rather than a score-driven game. Place five perched drone-like characters on glowing tree branches, with Sitrus at the center as the featured character. The main control scheme is simple tap or click input: tapping a character should spawn a floating chat bubble with one random line from that character's dialogue pool, play a chat sound, and briefly show a reaction card in the corner; tapping empty snow should create a small ripple particle burst with a softer reward sound. Tapping Sitrus should do all of that plus trigger a short glitch event with screen shake, red scanline flashes, a temporary HUD mood change from stable to glitched, harsher sound feedback, and a stronger reaction animation. Use a moody cyber-horror palette with deep midnight blues, cyan and magenta glow accents, gold highlights for Sitrus, subtle stars, a central glowing tree trunk, floating/bobbing characters, and glassy HUD panels. Keep the game responsive for mobile, preserve a minimalist presentation with no score, no fail state, and no levels, and make the loop about repeatedly discovering chatter, ambient reactions, and Sitrus's signature glitch personality.
